newsitem.title: FINLAND: NESTE UP SHARPLY ON IVO-MERGER SPECULATION.
newsitem.headline: NESTE UP SHARPLY ON IVO-MERGER SPECULATION.

text.p: Shares in Finnish oil, chemicals and energy group Neste rose sharply on Monday as speculation about a merger of Neste and unlisted state-owned power producer Imatran Voima (IVO) heated up anew, brokers said.
At 1355/1055 GMT, Neste traded at a year-high 144.00 markka, up 7.00 markka or 5.11 percent, bucking the overall downtrend.

Trade and Industry Minister Antti Kalliomaki was quoted as saying in business daily Kauppalehti that the government may force a merger of Neste and IVO if studies to be completed this month show that a merger would be rational.
Kalliomaki said the companies would be heard but that the project was up to the owners. The state owns 96 percent of IVO and 84 percent of Neste.
Neste's share could rise by 50 markka more in the next two months, one broker said.
The ministry of trade and industry on June 17 announced plans to study broadening state ownership in Neste and IVO, and options for joint development of the two, including a possible merger.
